1. Scope, evidence and mobile boundary

This is a source-extracted implementation handoff for the EDUwAI student question composer: Normal, Transliterate, Keyboard, Voice, transliteration language selection, transcript editing, and voice-question billing-period usage.

Documentation only: no web UI, backend, database, workflow, entitlement or provider setting is changed by this export. Native clients must consume the existing EDUwAI APIs, not duplicate the backend or database.

Statements marked Existing describe repository code. Recommended native describes a mobile adaptation, not shipped functionality. JSON examples are illustrative fixtures, not a live account. Source was inspected on 9 October 2026 (America/Chicago); installed/runtime provider settings and production health were not queried.

The attached screenshot is the visual evidence for the icon row. The signed-in composer was not exercised live. The PDF and HTML are offline references; the calculator in this HTML does not call any API.

Emoji artwork varies between Android, iOS, Windows and browser/font versions. There is no single shared vector source to extract for the four mode emojis. The screenshot remains the literal visual reference; Unicode identifies the semantic glyph, not exact artwork.

Recommended native: use one consistent icon set or custom approved SVGs: pen/writing, letters/language, keyboard, microphone. Keep text labels. SF Symbols and Material Symbols are platform options; Lucide is an optional cross-platform alternative, not the current toolbar dependency. Match the semantic meaning rather than claiming native symbols reproduce emoji artwork.

4. Modes and transition matrix

ActionExisting state changesText/network consequences
NormalInvalidate voice session; inputMode=normal; hide keyboard; clear transcript-ready/editing flags.Keeps question text. No input-mode API call.
TransliterateSame voice invalidation; mode=transliterate; hide keyboard; clear transcript flags.Keeps question; exposes language select; later Latin word input requests suggestions.
KeyboardInvalidate voice; mode=keyboard; toggle showKeyboard; clear transcript flags.Keeps question; keyboard component mounts only while shown.
Close keyboard XshowKeyboard=false only.Mode remains keyboard; text unchanged.
Voice tabmode=voice; hide keyboard; clear voiceError.Shows voice panel; does not auto-record or clear existing question.
Mic / Start recordingmode=voice; hide keyboard; start guarded recording flow.Usage refresh precedes permission request. Successful transcript replaces entire question.
Stop recordingStop timer; voiceTranscribing=true; MediaRecorder.stop().Finalized blob is uploaded after recorder onstop.
Edit transcript / Done editingToggle voiceTranscriptEditing.No transcription API call; no extra voice quota.

Voice invalidation increments a session fence, aborts its pending request, clears the timer, disconnects recorder handlers, stops recording and all microphone tracks. Stale responses are ignored. Voice tab itself differs from other tabs: it does not call invalidateVoiceTranscription. Native implementations should avoid duplicate recordings or accepting obsolete responses, without assuming an aborted client request guarantees no server-side quota consumption.

There is no combined “keyboard transliterate” mode in the current composer. The two are separate input methods; their language selections are independent.

5. Normal typing, text editing and shared submission

  • Normal uses the standard textarea/system keyboard. No transliteration or microphone API is called simply by typing.
  • Question textarea: four rows; 16px horizontal/12px vertical padding; 8px radius; no manual resize; focus ring 2px primary/20; unicodeBidi: plaintext.
  • Default placeholder: “e.g., What are the main relief features of India?”
  • Paste is intercepted: plain text only, normalized to NFC, inserted at selected range; caret moves after inserted text. Paste does not itself trigger transliteration suggestions.
  • The textarea is disabled during image question extraction, not universally while audio is transcribing.
  • Answer submission requires nonblank question and an active document. Choosing a mode never generates an answer.
Existing endpointJSON bodyNotes
POST /api/query/stream{"document_id":123,"question":"trimmed question","mode":"…"}Phase 1; Bearer token; consumes the existing answer flow.
POST /api/phase2/documents/{id}/query/stream{"question":"trimmed question","mode":"…"}Own materials; document ID in route.
POST /api/querySame Phase 1 body.Existing non-stream fallback after stream failure.
POST /api/phase2/documents/{id}/querySame own-material body.Existing non-stream fallback.

Preserve existing answer-mode values and stream protocol from the answer API. Input mode is not the answer API’s mode value. This handoff does not redefine retrieval, streaming, answer charging or TTS.

6. Transliteration: trigger, word boundaries and suggestions

  1. Set Transliterate and choose language (default Telugu).
  2. On text change, inspect selectionStart. Scan backward for whitespace or . ! ? , ; : - / newline; use text from boundary to cursor as currentWord.
  3. Only a nonempty word matching ^[a-zA-Z]+$ requests suggestions. Digits, punctuation and already-native script hide suggestions and clear currentWord.
  4. Client maps language to short code and sends the URL-encoded word to the backend proxy, with num_suggestions=5.
  5. Cache key = languageCode + “:” + lowercase word. Cached results avoid calls; cache uses insertion order and drops the oldest key beyond 10,000 entries, not true LRU.
  6. Returned candidates are copied; original word is appended if absent. Up to five provider suggestions may therefore produce six client options.
  7. Applying a suggestion replaces only the currentWord range, preserving text before/after; clears suggestion state; restores focus/caret.
GestureExisting action
Down / UpMove selected candidate with wraparound.
Enter / TabInsert selected candidate without automatically adding a trailing space.
SpaceInsert selected candidate plus a space when currentWord is nonempty.
1–5Insert corresponding candidate plus a space. A sixth original-word option cannot be selected via numeric shortcut 6.
Candidate tap/clickInsert candidate plus a space.
EscapeHide candidates.
Textarea blurHide after 200ms to allow suggestion click.

Candidate panel: absolute, z-index 50, left 16px, top 70px, margin-top 4px, max-width 24rem, border, 8px radius, shadow-lg. Row padding 16px × 8px, 12px internal gap; candidate font 18px / 28px; numbered badge 20×20px, 12px font.

Source caveats: no debounce, abort fence or response-order guard for transliteration; language change only updates state and does not proactively clear/refetch old suggestions. Cache is case-folded but retains originally appended word casing. HTTP success is not explicitly checked by fetch; proxy failure falls back to the original word, and the UI does not visibly distinguish success:false. Native recommendations: debounce, cancel stale queries, bind candidate responses to language/word/caret, preserve original text offline, and show recoverable network feedback.

Transliteration selector displays the above order. Keyboard pill order follows its layout object: Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Bengali, Gujarati, Marathi, Punjabi, Odia. Keyboard mounts with Hindi selected and default layout; transliteration begins with Telugu. Remounting the keyboard resets its local language/layout state.

Voice detects language server-side. Neither selected transliteration language nor keyboard language is sent with the audio. Voice has no language override field in this API. Transliteration placeholder always uses a Hindi “namaste → नमस्ते” example even with another language selected; do not interpret it as the target language contract.

8. Transliteration API contract and upstream

GET /api/transliterate/{lang}/{word}?num_suggestions=5

Path lang is one of hi, te, ta, kn, ml, bn, gu, mr, pa, or. Encode the word as a URL path component. The route shown has no get_current_user dependency; the existing fetch call sends no explicit Authorization header. No per-user monthly transcription/answer quota is reserved by transliteration.

GET /api/transliterate/te/namaste?num_suggestions=5
Success shape: {"result":["candidate 1","candidate 2"],"success":true}
Provider failure: {"result":["namaste"],"success":false}
Timeout: {"result":["namaste"],"success":false,"error":"Request timeout"}

The backend performs GET https://inputtools.google.com/request with text=word, itc=language input method, num=num_suggestions, cp=0, cs=1, ie=utf-8, oe=utf-8; timeout 5 seconds. It reads Google’s nested SUCCESS candidate array and returns a simpler result list.

Unsupported language codes currently fall back to Hindi rather than rejecting. num_suggestions is typed as integer but has no explicit range clamp here. Exceptions usually return a success-status JSON fallback, not an HTTP transport failure.

Despite AI4Bharat identifiers/comments in the frontend, the implemented provider is Google Input Tools. This proxy is not Google Translate translation and is not an Indic transliteration SDK integrated into the client. No SLA or licensing assurance was established by inspecting code; review provider terms before a separate mobile launch.

Client route currently uses config.backendUrl + /api, so it targets the configured API host even in places where other calls use a local proxy. Native clients should use the approved environment-specific EDUwAI API origin consistently, not call Google directly.

7699: @app.get("/api/transliterate/{lang}/{word}")
7700: def transliterate_word(lang: str, word: str, num_suggestions: int = 5):
7701:     """
7702:     Proxy endpoint for Google Input Tools transliteration API.
7703:     Same quality as Google Translate's input method.
7704:     
7705:     Supported languages: hi (Hindi), te (Telugu), ta (Tamil), kn (Kannada),
7706:     ml (Malayalam), bn (Bengali), gu (Gujarati), mr (Marathi), pa (Punjabi), or (Odia)
7707:     """
7708:     # Note: 'requests' is imported at top of file for production reliability
7709:     
7710:     # Google Input Tools language codes
7711:     google_lang_codes = {
7712:         'hi': 'hi-t-i0-und',  # Hindi
7713:         'te': 'te-t-i0-und',  # Telugu
7714:         'ta': 'ta-t-i0-und',  # Tamil
7715:         'kn': 'kn-t-i0-und',  # Kannada
7716:         'ml': 'ml-t-i0-und',  # Malayalam
7717:         'bn': 'bn-t-i0-und',  # Bengali
7718:         'gu': 'gu-t-i0-und',  # Gujarati
7719:         'mr': 'mr-t-i0-und',  # Marathi
7720:         'pa': 'pa-t-i0-und',  # Punjabi
7721:         'or': 'or-t-i0-und',  # Odia
7722:     }
7723:     
7724:     itc = google_lang_codes.get(lang, 'hi-t-i0-und')
7725:     
7726:     try:
7727:         response = requests.get(
7728:             "https://inputtools.google.com/request",
7729:             params={
7730:                 "text": word,
7731:                 "itc": itc,
7732:                 "num": num_suggestions,
7733:                 "cp": 0,
7734:                 "cs": 1,
7735:                 "ie": "utf-8",
7736:                 "oe": "utf-8"
7737:             },
7738:             timeout=5
7739:         )
7740:         data = response.json()
7741:         
7742:         # Google returns: ["SUCCESS", [["word", ["suggestion1", "suggestion2", ...], ...]]]
7743:         if data[0] == "SUCCESS" and len(data) > 1 and len(data[1]) > 0:
7744:             suggestions = data[1][0][1]  # Array of transliterated suggestions
7745:             return {"result": suggestions, "success": True}
7746:         else:
7747:             return {"result": [word], "success": False}
7748:     except requests.exceptions.Timeout:
7749:         print(f"⚠️ Transliteration timeout for word '{word}' in {lang}")
7750:         return {"result": [word], "success": False, "error": "Request timeout"}
7751:     except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError as e:
7752:         print(f"❌ Transliteration connection error: {e}")
7753:         return {"result": [word], "success": False, "error": "Connection failed - check network access"}
7754:     except Exception as e:
7755:         print(f"❌ Transliteration API error for '{word}' ({lang}): {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
7756:         return {"result": [word], "success": False, "error": str(e)}

9. Virtual keyboard panel and styles

Existing: simple-keyboard renders a fixed bottom panel spanning viewport width, z-index 50, shadow-2xl and top border. Inner max-width is 56rem (896px), centered, 12px padding. Header is a flex row with wrapping language buttons and close X; 12px bottom margin.

ElementLightDark / primary theme
PanelWhite; border-gray-200.Gray-900 #111827; border-gray-700 #374151.
Language label14px / 20px, medium; gray-600.Gray-300.

Function keymax-width80px; backspace and enter max-width100px.Same.
Spacemax-width400px; flex-grow1.Same.

Keyboard library is created/destroyed when selected language, layoutName or theme changes. It does not own the full question buffer: onChange is a no-op; onKeyPress dispatches typed events to the parent. No keyboard API call, subscription request or transcription occurs when pressing a key.

Recommended native: account for safe-area/IME overlap, avoid double system+custom keyboards, let the question remain visible, and preserve screen-reader key labels. Use grapheme-aware deletion rather than copying the current UTF-16 deletion limitation.

10. Keyboard actions, symbols and exact layouts

KeyDisplay / outputExisting semantics
{shift} / {lock}⇧ / ⇪Both toggle default↔shift. No distinct caps-lock persistence behavior.
{bksp}⌫Parent question.slice(0,-1): removes final UTF-16 code unit, not cursor selection or whole grapheme.
{enter}↵Append newline.
{tab}⇥Append tab character, not move focus.
{space}Blank spacebarAppend a space.
Other keysNative character or .com / @ etc.Append button value at end of entire question; focus textarea.

These layouts are custom arrays in IndianLanguageKeyboard.jsx, not imported from simple-keyboard-layouts. They are not certified OS/standard InScript layouts. All ten include five rows in default and shift variants. Some keys output conjunct sequences; the exact strings below are the source of truth.

Important parity limitations: key insertion and backspace operate at the end, not the current caret/selection; deletion can break surrogate pairs and Indic combining sequences. Native behavior should be explicitly approved if improved rather than silently described as existing.

11. Voice recording lifecycle and limits

  1. Voice tab reveals panel. Start recording or bottom Mic invokes guarded flow; do not record just because the tab becomes active.
  2. Block duplicate start, active recording or transcribing. If cached usage says disallowed, show billing-period quota notice.
  3. Invalidate previous session, reset transcript flags/error/language/timer; load authoritative usage again before permission.
  4. Require getUserMedia and MediaRecorder; request audio:true. Denied permission yields recoverable message; unsupported browser offers typed-question fallback.
  5. Try browser-native MediaRecorder(stream) first; otherwise try MP4/AAC then WebM/Opus and Ogg/Opus supported formats.
  6. Collect nonempty chunks; compute elapsed wall-clock seconds, update display every 250ms; auto-stop at 60 seconds.
  7. On stop, stop all microphone tracks. Use recorder MIME or chunk MIME and finalize Blob before upload. Empty blob errors without paid transcription.
  8. Client duration is ceil(elapsed) clamped to 1–60. Backend separately probes actual audio duration; client-reported duration is not trusted for length enforcement.
  9. Reject client blob over 10×1024×1024 bytes. Upload audio and integer duration_seconds as multipart.
  10. Successful response overwrites the question with trimmed transcript, exposes formatted preview and detected language, and updates returned usage. No automatic answer submission.

There is no audio storage/replay UI in this flow. The backend reads audio in request memory and states it never persists the recording. Temporary validation/provider processing still occurs; provider retention policy was not verified.

LimitExisting value
Audio duration1–60 declared seconds; actual decoded duration must not exceed60.
Audio bytes10,485,760 maximum audio bytes (10MiB; user copy says10MB).
Whole multipart request10MiB +64KiB framing allowance via middleware.
Short request rate12 admitted transcription attempts in10 minutes, including failed provider attempts.
Provider stage deadline40s for transcription; interactions formatter has its own40s deadline, so two-stage total may exceed40s.
Provider retryAt most2 attempts per stage; transient retry delay0.75s; original quota reservation reused.

13. Voice API: authenticated multipart request

POST /api/transcribe-voice-question

Requires authenticated student via Bearer token. Existing axios client includes token and credentials, refresh handling and institute context where appropriate. Mobile must reuse the app’s auth/session scheme; never embed provider keys.

Authorization: Bearer <student_access_token>
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=<generated by HTTP library>

audio: binary file, e.g. voice-question.m4a, media type audio/mp4
duration_seconds: "12" (integer form field, not JSON)

Response example:
{
  "transcript": "What is the value of $x^2$?",
  "detected_language": "en",
  "voice_question_usage": {
    "used": 3,
    "limit": 10,
    "remaining": 7,
    "allowed": true
  }
}

Do not force application/json and do not manually omit the multipart boundary. A successful transcription’s usage object does not include period_end; fetch the usage endpoint when expiry is needed. Detected language is a provider-produced string, not an enforced ISO-only enumeration; empty string becomes “und”. No language, document_id or question-answer mode field belongs in this transcription request.

Canonical accepted MIMEAliases / native hints
audio/webm, audio/oggWebM/Opus, Ogg/Opus; codec suffix normalized.
audio/mp4audio/x-m4a, audio/m4a, video/mp4, application/mp4 normalize to audio/mp4; .m4a expected for AAC-in-MP4.
audio/aacaudio/x-aac → audio/aac; .aac extension.
audio/mpegaudio/mp3 → audio/mpeg; .mp3 extension.
audio/wav, audio/x-wav, audio/waveWAV accepted; size limit still applies.

Server validates headers/body size, normalizes MIME and supported extensions, validates declared duration, reads max bytes+1, probes actual duration using ffprobe, checks provider configuration, then reserves usage. Do not upload compressed audio under an inaccurate MIME or filename. A native recorder should reliably finalize its file before POST.

14. Voice API errors, retries and cancellation

Status / conditionMeaningClient response
400Empty/unreadable recording, invalid duration, probe timeout.Discard invalid recording; explain and rerecord; no reservation before validation succeeds.
401Expired/missing student auth.Use existing refresh/login mechanism; never bypass entitlement.
413Audio >10MiB or request body cap.Shorter/lower-bitrate recording; do not retry same oversized body.
415Unsupported media format.Choose supported native container/MIME.
422No speech; malformed required form fields can also produce FastAPI422.Rerecord silence; repair multipart for validation errors. Array details map to incomplete-upload message.
429 quotaAllowance exhausted for current billing period.Disable record; preserve typing; show period expiry from usage API.
429 rateToo many attempts in10 minutes; provider errors can also classify as rate issues.Wait/retry without assuming monthly quota is exhausted. No Retry-After contract established.
503Missing configuration/SDK or provider unavailability, depending classifier.Recoverable service error; reconcile usage; do not expose keys.
504Stage deadline exceeded.Suggest shorter question; reconcile usage; avoid immediate duplicate POST.
Network / cancellationNo authoritative response may have reached client.Ignore stale transcript; GET usage to reconcile; abort does not prove the server never processed audio.

Server releases failed reservations by reclassifying the event as voice_transcription_failed. Internal transient provider retry uses one reservation. Successful transcriptions still consume voice quota even if the student never submits the resulting question. Failed pre-validation requests need not enter the same rate-event counter; do not claim every HTTP attempt is logged.

The frontend uses server detail strings first; array detail → incomplete-upload message; missing response → connection notice; other5xx → temporarily-busy notice. Failure refreshes usage. Session fences suppress response updates after mode changes, new recording, document changes or unmount.

15. Voice provider architecture and prompt policy

All paid/provider work is server-side. Mobile integrates with EDUwAI transcription, not directly with Gemini, Vertex, Google Cloud credentials or an external speech SDK. Active model and auth transport are admin-controlled; this export does not claim a current production model.

  • Standard generation: configured model via Vertex AI or Gemini API key; instruction accompanies audio; expects JSON transcript and detected_language.
  • Interactions: requires API-key mode and an approved dedicated transcription model; literal output is then passed to a separate configured standard formatter. Requires google-genai with client.interactions support.
  • Saved prompt preserves Indian-language and mixed-language speech without translation, transcribes only (never solves), formats clear STEM notation as LaTeX and leaves non-STEM text plain.
  • Formatting failure is not a successful transcription; quota reservation is released. Two stages and retries can increase provider cost without adding more successful voice-question units.
  • Do not hardcode mobile provider model, region or prompt. No provider secret belongs in the handoff or app bundle.

Server requirements: FastAPI, python-multipart, requests (transliteration), database/SQLAlchemy usage accounting, ffprobe for audio validation, google-genai for API-key/Interactions and Google Cloud Vertex SDK path for Vertex mode. These are backend dependencies, not packages a native UI team must reproduce.

16. Billing-period quota API and allowance rules

GET /api/billing/voice-question-usage

Authorization: Bearer <student_access_token>
{
  "used": 3,
  "limit": 10,
  "remaining": 7,
  "allowed": true,
  "period_end": "2026-11-09T00:00:00"
}

Timestamp above is illustrative, not an actual expiry. The backend may serialize a nullable datetime; parse defensively and apply the backend’s UTC convention without assuming the string includes an offset. No period_start field is returned by this endpoint.

RuleExisting contract
Balanceremaining=max(0,limit-used); allowed=(used<limit). Never compute entitlement only from a mobile hardcoded plan.
Free fallback10 per billing period if no configured tier limit. Admin may change limit, including explicit0.
Institute-paidOrganization voice_question_limit_per_student, per student, fallback10; independent of old personal-paid record.
Institute individual-paidOrganization-scoped tier; scoped free tier preferred, then global free fallback.
Consumer paidLive current tier entitlement at request time; stored allocation fallback only if tier absent.
YearlyCurrent paid yearly quota = monthly tier quota×14 for the yearly billing period. Not12 and not a fresh monthly reset.
Free / institute periodsMonthly anniversary windows; on-demand/hourly reset; not necessarily calendar months.
Individual paid periodsPayment renewal authoritative; do not automatically reset on phone calendar change.
Accountingvoice_transcription reserves one unit before model call; failed event reclassified and excluded from monthly used, retained for admitted-attempt rate limit.
Concurrent requestsUser-row lock serializes quota check/reservation. Temporary in-flight reservations can appear in used.
Separate limitsVoice-question quota is distinct from answer-question count and tutor voice explanation/TTS allowance.

Usage is loaded on portal mount, before recording and after failed POST; success POST supplies updated balance. Typing, virtual-key presses, transliteration, preview or transcript editing do not consume voice allowance. Later answering the transcript follows normal answer billing independently.

17. Monthly voice-question estimator: scope and formulas

Existing vs export-only: the web composer currently shows billing-period remaining/limit; no independent monthly forecasting calculator was found in this flow. The calculator below is a planning utility added only to this exported HTML, not to the web app.

Student balance planning: use authoritative used U, period limit L, days left D. Remaining R=max(0,L−U). Planned successful transcriptions = ceil(daily target×D). Additional successful requests actually available = min(R,planned). Estimated exhaustion = R/daily target (if target>0). For yearly subscriptions, L is an annual pool; do not label all L as “monthly quota”. If days left≤0, refresh entitlement instead of assuming allowance resets.

Institution/month capacity: N active students, Q intended successful voice questions/student/month, S mean seconds/question (1–60), p first-attempt success fraction (0<p≤1). Successful questions=N×Q. Audio minutes for successes=N×Q×S/60. Expected client attempts=successful/p. Approximate uploaded audio minutes including failed attempts=successful×S/(60×p), assuming similar mean duration on failures.

Optional cost estimate: if the finance team provides an effective USD/audio-minute rate r, approximate audio cost=attempt audio minutes×r. Add formatter token cost, internal provider retries, text/prompt tokens, storage/network/infrastructure, taxes and exchange rate separately. An effective rate is a planning assumption, not provider pricing fetched by this document.

The reservation code initializes cost_usd, tokens_input and tokens_output to0; this endpoint does not return a verified transcription invoice or cost meter. Do not infer actual provider spending is zero. No current Gemini/Vertex price or currency conversion has been asserted.

Illustrative monthSuccessful questionsSuccess audio minutesAt80% first-attempt success
100 students ×10 questions ×15sec1,0002501,250 attempts;312.5 attempt-audio minutes.
500 students ×20 questions ×30sec10,0005,00012,500 attempts;6,250 attempt-audio minutes.
1,000 students ×10 questions ×60sec10,00010,00012,500 attempts;12,500 attempt-audio minutes.

These are workload examples, not confirmed tier allowances. A10-unit free period permits10 successful transcriptions, not10 attempts or10 audio minutes. With L=10,U=3,D=14,daily target1, only7 additional successes are available; depletion in about7days.

Offline monthly planning calculator (export-only)

Default scenario:1,000 successful questions;250 success-audio minutes;1,250 estimated client attempts;312.5 attempt-audio minutes. Cost not estimated: no approved rate entered.

HTML inputs update offline. PDF captures this default scenario; it is not interactive. No account IDs or recorded audio are needed.

Web version ranges are copied from package.json, not a mobile installation manifest. Native recommendations are options, not existing integrations or pinned compatible versions. Avoid shipping deprecated recorder packages without checking the selected platform SDK documentation. No package install is part of this export.

19. Native implementation sequence and acceptance checklist

  1. Choose shared input state: text, selection, inputMode, selected transliteration language, keyboard language/layout, candidates, recording state, session fence, authoritative usage.
  2. Implement mode row and clear selected labels. Support accessibility, focus, safe areas, dark/light theme and44/48 native touch targets.
  3. Direct typing and paste must preserve Unicode and caret selection; do not transliterate speech or existing native script automatically.
  4. Wire transliteration proxy only for Latin word input; retain original word on failure; add request ordering and language binding as deliberate native improvements.
  5. Render custom language layouts or explicitly approve system keyboard alternative. Confirm Unicode combining marks and conjunct keys with fluent language testers.
  6. Load voice quota via existing authenticated client. Start recording only after explicit action and entitlement check. Record1–60sec in backend-supported audio format.
  7. Finalize multipart file, send duration_seconds integer, handle each error state, preserve edits, ignore stale responses and clean up microphone resources.
  8. Display editable/formatted transcript without auto-solving; use existing answer APIs only after explicit submission.

Minimum test matrix

  • All4 tabs switch, preserve text and have appropriate active state; keyboard X closes; mode panel fits small screen and landscape.
  • Each of10 languages: selector code, sample phonetic word, candidate tap, Space/Enter/Tab/arrows/1–5/Escape, original-word fallback, cache and no-network path.
  • Typing in middle/selection replacement, punctuation, digits, newlines, paste NFC, mixed script; rapid language/word changes cannot insert stale candidates.
  • All default/shift layouts; shift/lock toggles; tab/enter/space/.com; approved grapheme-aware deletion and caret behavior.
  • Permission granted/denied/permanently denied, unsupported recorder, zero audio, exact1sec/exact60sec/over60 decoded audio,10MiB boundary, wrong MIME and finalized MP4/AAC on iOS.
  • Transcript ready → Edit → Done; STEM LaTeX, Indian scripts, mixed language, blank speech, unsafe markup; no unwanted translation or answering.
  • Concurrent start taps, switch mode during upload, navigate/unmount, document change, cancelled client whose server completed; quota reconciliation.
  • Free/institute/individual/yearly, limit0, used=limit−1 versus used=limit,12/10min attempt cap, provider failure quota release, tier edit applying immediately, anniversary expiry and annual pool.
  • Offline planner values1–60sec, valid success fraction, no approved cost rate, zero planned questions; native client does not reinterpret planner output as entitlement.

783: def _tier_voice_question_limit(tier: Optional[SubscriptionTier]) -> int:
784:     """Return a safe voice-question allowance from a tier, including zero."""
785:     if tier and tier.voice_question_limit is not None:
786:         return max(0, int(tier.voice_question_limit))
787:     return FREE_VOICE_QUESTION_LIMIT
788: 
789: 
790: def get_voice_question_limit(db: Session, user_id: int) -> int:
791:     """Return the current-billing-period transcription allowance for a student.
792: 
793:     Institute-pay organisations use their per-student allowance. Individual-pay
794:     organisations use the student's organisation-scoped tier; consumer users use
795:     global tiers. This intentionally does not share the tutor voice-explain limit.
796:     """
797:     org = _get_user_org(db, user_id)
798:     if org and getattr(org, "payment_type", None) == "institute":
799:         configured_limit = getattr(org, "voice_question_limit_per_student", None)
800:         return max(0, int(configured_limit)) if configured_limit is not None else FREE_VOICE_QUESTION_LIMIT
801: 
802:     sub = db.query(UserSubscription).filter(UserSubscription.user_id == user_id).first()
803:     if not sub or sub.tier_slug in ("free", None) or sub.status == "past_due":
804:         free_tier_query = db.query(SubscriptionTier).filter(SubscriptionTier.slug == "free")
805:         if org and getattr(org, "payment_type", None) == "individual":
806:             # Prefer an institute's own free tier when it has one; otherwise
807:             # retain the platform's consumer free allowance as the fallback.
808:             free_tier = free_tier_query.filter(SubscriptionTier.org_id == org.id).first()
809:             if not free_tier:
810:                 free_tier = free_tier_query.filter(SubscriptionTier.org_id == None).first()
811:         else:
812:             free_tier = free_tier_query.filter(SubscriptionTier.org_id == None).first()
813:         return _tier_voice_question_limit(free_tier)
814: 
815:     tier = _get_subscription_tier(db, user_id, sub.tier_slug)
816:     limit = _assigned_or_current_tier_quota(
817:         sub,
818:         "allocated_voice_question_limit",
819:         tier.voice_question_limit if tier else None,
820:     )
821:     if tier is None and getattr(sub, "allocated_voice_question_limit", None) is None:
822:         return FREE_VOICE_QUESTION_LIMIT
823:     return limit
824: 
825: 
826: def get_voice_question_count(
827:     db: Session,
828:     user_id: int,
829:     billing_period_str: str,
830:     period_start=None,
831: ) -> int:
832:     """Count reserved voice-question transcriptions in the current billing period."""
833:     try:
834:         query = """
835:             SELECT COUNT(*) FROM usage_events
836:             WHERE user_id = :uid
837:             AND question_type = 'voice_transcription'
838:             AND billing_period = :period
839:         """
840:         params = {"uid": user_id, "period": billing_period_str}
841:         if period_start:
842:             query += " AND created_at >= :period_start"
843:             params["period_start"] = period_start
844:         row = db.execute(text(query), params).fetchone()
845:         return row[0] if row else 0
846:     except Exception as e:
847:         logger.error(f"Voice question count query failed for user {user_id}: {e}")
848:         return 0
849:

851: def get_voice_question_usage_summary(db: Session, user_id: int) -> dict:
852:     """Return the authenticated student's current transcription allowance."""
853:     _get_or_create_subscription(db, user_id)
854:     period_start, period_end, billing_period = get_current_billing_period(db, user_id)
855:     limit = get_voice_question_limit(db, user_id)
856:     used = get_voice_question_count(db, user_id, billing_period, period_start)
857:     return {
858:         "used": used,
859:         "limit": limit,
860:         "remaining": max(0, limit - used),
861:         "allowed": used < limit,
862:         "period_end": period_end,
863:     }
